working_title: Common decline, divergent collapse: breeding-colony network structure predicts local resilience across Antarctic penguin islands
one_sentence_claim: Across neighboring Antarctic breeding islands, Adelie populations share an exceptionally strong long-term decline but differ in short-term dynamics and extinction, and modest held-out-year resilience information lies in how breeders are distributed among subcolonies rather than in simple sea-ice-duration, annual snowfall, or large-group-retention metrics.

evidence_roles.exploratory_palmer_penguins: motivation only: apparent island morphology is mainly compositional and within-Adelie island phenotype is temporally labile
evidence_roles.apbp_local_network: assembly endpoint context: vacancy, persistence, and non-island gentoo replacement are heterogeneous
evidence_roles.seaice_annual_and_timescale: prospective falsification of simple regional forcing formulations
evidence_roles.snowfall_x_habitat: prospective falsification of simple annual terrestrial-weather moderation
evidence_roles.external_50_pair_threshold: external historical hypothesis validation showing colony-network diversity is not equivalent to large-group retention

primary_claims: Five nearby Adelie island populations share a dominant same-sign long-term decline, but annual demographic synchrony is only moderate and extinction endpoints differ.
Simple annual sea-ice duration, 3/5/7-year duration summaries, and October snowfall x static snow-prone habitat do not explain the pattern in their predeclared directions with held-out validation.
Effective colony number provides a small positive held-out-year increment beyond current abundance, island identity and secular time trend.
The colony-network result is not reducible to the number of occupied colonies or to retaining more >50-pair groups.
Broader Palmer breeding sites show heterogeneous assembly outcomes rather than uniform species replacement.
prohibited_claims: sea ice is unimportant to Adelie penguins
all Palmer islands undergo the same replacement process
Biscoe Point is a true small-island replicate
within-Adelie morphology differences demonstrate local adaptation
the supported colony-network gain explains the dominant regional decline
manuscript_order: system: externally subsidized breeding islands separate marine resources from terrestrial breeding patches
assembly context: apparent island trait structure is dominated by species composition and long-term endpoints differ among breeding sites
primary result: near-common five-island Adelie decline with only moderate annual synchrony
falsification: simple marine-duration and annual snowfall mechanisms fail prospective transfer tests
local state: effective colony-network diversity provides modest positive next-year predictive information
specificity: active colony count fails and the external >50-pair directional hypothesis reverses
synthesis: regional direction and local collapse are different ecological scales

terminal_development_rule: Do not open another climate window, precipitation month, colony-size threshold or topology index for the core paper. New work must be external validation, figure/reproducibility work, or clearly separate future research.
